extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in computational linguistics, AI for social sciences & humanities, and educational technologists
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, pretraining, evaluating, and building user interfaces for causal language models tailored to the social sciences and humanities (SSH), with attention to disciplinary norms and educational use. Includes creating SSH-specific benchmarks and interface designs that preserve critical engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causal language models fully pretrained by and for the social sciences and humanities (SSH)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The SHARE models are the first causal language models fully pretrained by and for the social sciences and humanities (SSH)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models should be pretrained on SSH-specific data and crafted with SSH needs in mind (rather than being generic models fine-tuned for SSH). Emphasises domain-specific pretraining as a primary desideratum for model relevance to SSH research and education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance in modelling SSH texts (SSH Cloze benchmark)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Their performance in modelling SSH texts is close to that of general purpose models (Phi-4) ... as shown by our custom SSH Cloze benchmark."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate models using SSH-specific benchmarks (here, a custom SSH Cloze benchmark) and compare against general-purpose baselines. Benchmark performance on SSH tasks is a central criterion for model suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Token/data efficiency relative to general-purpose models
rubrics_metrics.description: "...which use 100 times more tokens" (contrast used to show SHARE's performance given much less pretraining data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value models that achieve comparable SSH performance with substantially less pretraining data/tokens. Token efficiency and data-efficiency are important evaluation axes and selling points when arguing practical benefits of SSH-focused pretraining.

rubrics_metrics.name: User interface design that preserves critical engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: "The MIRROR user interface is designed for reviewing text inputs from the SSH disciplines while preserving critical engagement."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interfaces for SSH use should support review and critical assessment of AI outputs rather than uncritical consumption. Design decisions should foreground tools and affordances that help users interrogate, contextualise, and critique model-derived information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-generative (review-only) generative-AI interface to protect disciplinary integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: "By prototyping a generative AI interface that does not generate any text, we propose a way to harness the capabilities of the SHARE models without compromising the integrity of SSH principles and norms."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer interface modalities that harness model capabilities (e.g., highlighting, critique, suggestions) without producing new fluent text that might bypass SSH norms. Protecting disciplinary integrity and norms is a stated design constraint; the interface should avoid automated text generation when that risks undermining SSH principles.
